# Store calls inside loops in business/, controllers/ and domain/, as they were when
# helpers/storeLoopGuard_test.go landed (backend audit, 18 Oct 2026): file :: function :: call.
# Batch a loop, then delete its line. A new line needs a reason in its commit.
# 20 Oct 2026, integrator: the BE-FOUND stack's stricter walk, merged onto beta 18bb5be5,
# found the store calls in loops that had landed since it was cut (calendar, calls, hooks,
# publish, task writer, workflow); they are recorded here as they are, to be batched by their owners.
# 20 Oct 2026, CHAT-LEAD: the chat stack's loops that run per item by nature: a message's two
# outbox events (live, the rest; as business/Post's writer), one live event for each reaction taken
# back (an app reads them one at a time; usually one), the one-off thread adoption sweep (two kinds,
# a page of roots at a time, each root with its own people) and the demo seed's showcase reactions.
# 20 Oct 2026, CHAT-LEAD: an import's pins are read a page of the graph's read limit (MaxRead) at a time.
# 20 Oct 2026, CHAT-LEAD: the Slack import's reaction pass is one writer for every kind of conversation: a message's
# target is read once (writerFor), each emoji and each person once a pass (cached), and each reaction is one write by Reaction's rule.
# 21 Oct 2026, CAL-LEAD-2: the calendar stack's loops that run per item by nature. An import
# writes each event through the one write path (the event, its instances, guests and reminders in
# one transaction, so a bad one is skipped alone), into a calendar found or made by name for each
# calendar in the file (a handful). A move from Google pulls each of a link's calendars whole (a
# handful), then keeps that calendar's refs, its ledger row and the progress bar. Two-way sync runs
# per link (each its own account and token, at most syncLinksPerSweep a sweep), per calendar of a
# link (each its own pull and cursor), and per pushed event (one Google call each, its ref kept at
# once so a sweep cut short never sends an event twice). A pulled change reads its event as the
# page's earlier writes left it, then writes it with its own later-wins check; the page's refs are
# kept and dropped once. Many calendars' chips read their next events once.
# 21 Oct 2026, CAL-LEAD-2 (B8 subscriptions): the import's loops live in importFiles, which takes
# a target calendar. A subscription sweep reads each due subscription on its own (each its own claimed
# address read, at most subscriptionsPerSweep). A changed file's events are read in one go and their
# refs kept once; each changed event is then its own write, and its instances read the series again
# each time, because skipping one changes it. Adopting events a cut-short read left is a rare repair.
# 21 Oct 2026, CALLS-LEAD (HU13): a link that ends puts out the members who came in by it as
# themselves, each checked once (MemberMayBeInCall: their conversation, meeting or another link) and
# put out once; neither has a batch call, and one link lets in a few people.
# 22 Oct 2026, WHITEBOARD-LEAD-3: the Miro import (W-2) reads Miro by its own pages: boards, items,
# connectors and groups by cursor, tags by offset and the items of each tag, and an item's style one
# at a time where the list leaves it out (Miro has no read by ids), with a 429's wait between tries.
# A board's pictures are fetched and kept one at a time, as a paste is (each scanned and within the
# upload limit), each kept picture's id mapping is written on its own (there is no batch upsert), and
# a rollback deletes each imported board through the board's own delete (its drawing, versions and files).
# 22 Oct 2026: Linear's issue lists page from the issue itself after their first page
# (a cursor per page; only issues with more than the first page ask, since one query with every list was over
# Linear's complexity cap). They are Linear's API calls, a page at a time by nature, not store reads.
# 23 Oct 2026, DOCS-LEAD-7 (N1 gap 1): a copied body's mentions are kept before its seed, one doc at a time
# beside the seed each loop already makes per doc (Duplicate's copies, an import's pages, parents first).
# 23 Oct 2026: Jira's sprints are searched a project at a time, before its tasks come (a project
# makes its cycles first): Jira's API, one search each, with at most one warning a project of each kind. Each project's
# sprints are kept for the job, so the projects' stage tried again neither searches nor warns about one read before.
# 24 Oct 2026: a task list's CSV in its Manual order reads its tasks a page of ReadAllPage
# uids at a time (manualRows), at most ten pages, so a long list is written as it is read and never held whole.
# 24 Oct 2026, CHAT-LEAD-22: a share reads which files a page of its source conversation's messages
# holds in one read (= ANY over the page's file ids, keepConversationFiles), once a page of sharePageSize.
# 24 Oct 2026, CHAT-LEAD-22: the "/" catalog reads each installed app's secret bag at most once (memoised
# in bags) to place that app's commands: one read for each of the handful of apps the workspace installed.
# 24 Oct 2026, TABLES-LEAD-26: an AI column's fill reads its own state (one row by its key) before each
# cell it asks the model for (fillRun.mayGoOn), so Stop ends it within a cell; each read stands beside a model call.
# 25 Oct 2026, CHAT-LEAD-27: the DM list's one-off backfill (DG4) stamps older DMs a batch of 500 at a time, at most 200 batches a run; each batch is one upsert.
# 25 Oct 2026, CALLS-LEAD-10 (calls package A): the sweep writes each ended call's report of its polls and questions under that call's own claim, at most 50 calls a pass: one claim and one reply a call, by nature.
# 29 Oct 2026, TABLES-LEAD-69 (TABLES-LEAD-70: none a field at a time): the Computed Store's fill and sweep (airtable-03) run a batch of rows or a table at a time, as IndexTable does: a fill's batches of rows (fillKept, IndexTable's .fill) and the sweep's tables (at most 20 to fill and 10 with rows waiting a round, each with its own fields and marks). A fill marks all of its table's fields in one statement, and what each reaches comes from the one plan of their table.
